children: impressed analysts with its investor day event this week. During the event, the company detailed how it reached a critical inflection point, driven by proven software, scalable hardware, an accelerating supply ramp, and strong customer demand.
Oppenheimer analyst Colin Rusch said the investor day showcased the commercial preparedness of Aurora's
technology platform and the willingness of its customers to support accelerated adoption. In terms of financial guidance, Rusch said the 2027 revenue target from Aurora
was slightly ahead of Street expectations but that the 2030 revenue and EBIT targets suggest more than 50% upside to Street estimates.

Needham reiterated its Buy rating on the stock after the company offered "sturdier support beams" to underwrite longer-dated estimates. Analyst Chris Pierce pointed to his team's confidence in the technology, the pace of industry adoption, and the broader autonomous trucking thesis. While new OEM relationships or new partner truck orders did not materialize, the firm sees plenty of room to increase patience levels for bulls with updated 2030 estimates still well ahead of prior consensus.

Morgan Stanley analyst Ravi Shanker highlighted that confidence was a key theme of the event despite the lack of headline announcements from management. "We got powerful validation from key fleet, OEM, T1 hardware, and insurance partners that the path forward needed practical blocking and tackling rather than resolving any key gating factors/unresolved questions," noted Shanker.
fell 6.3% in Thursday afternoon trading amid broad weakness in technology names. The stock is still up more than 55% on a year-to-date basis.
